The dealership has replaced the battery at least once. As far as we know the service department cannot diagnose the problem and has only been able to repeat it once. We have never been given a reason for the repeated loss of power, even when the battery is fully charged. The dealership has not contacted us in almost a week and we have not been given an update on the status of the car. We are fed up, the car is unfixable and we would like to explore legal options under Oregon's Lemon Law, as it applies, even though we live in Vancouver.

vars.problem_description: Been a sprint/tmobile customer for many years. Yesterday I was about to buy 2 phones. It was a process. When we were finished got home with 2 new phones. My fiance couldn't use the new phone as she could hardly see the screen. So we called tmobile customer service and the gentleman said they were going to refund the restocking fee. It was my account so we (2 of us) was on the phone with the gentleman & heard what he said. He stated he will put a note our files and we could just go to the nearest store and return the phone & get another phone. When we got to the store, the lady read the gentleman's notes and he stated that he told us we couldn't get the restocking fee waived, & that we understood. That was a lie.....I am now angry & they won't give us back the money for any transaction. I am very upset that TMOBILE is doing this to their customers and it needs to stop. I just want my $ back.

prompt.raw: I am seeking a consultation for a lawyer in regards to injuries I got on the job that I feel were preventable if my supervisor had listened to me. It wasn't a sudden onset injury but developed over time, I went to my lead when it became obvious something was wrong. He blew it off saying I was just tired. After a couple months I went back to him again complaining of pain, he blew it off. Over 18 months I went to him 5 times before he told me I needed a doctor's note, I went to the doctor the next day and was immediately put on light duty. My supervisor tried saying that I didn't come to him "officially" but there's no "official" procedure. There's a giant sign in the breakroom saying "if you are injured, no matter small, tell your supervisor." Eventually I was moved to another department and after 30 days was laid off with 43 other people. I have had 2 surgeries, with another on the way. Am in constant pain, have limitations on my primary arm and more. Thank you

While they are actively recruiting for people all the time, they have assured her that it is her sole responsiblity to fill the vacancy. We are so far unable to fill it. We would like to put this behind us, but we can't. To make matters worse, I've heard from others, and read reviews that Ducks Village is not a nice place to live. So, despite the fact that we gave them 8 months notice before actual move in date, we are currently stuck with a $12,000 lease. What can we do? The only leg I feel we have to stand on is that they are required to search for her, and they are clearly not doing that.
